timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The civilization thrives usually on two things.
Access to water and access to arable land.
If you don't have food and water, then a human civilization will effectively be on survival mode all the time.
At Manhat, we develop a technology that will allow us to produce water without electricity
and by extension we do not emit CO2 and we do not produce prime.
Our focus at this stage, frankly speaking, is on providing water for irrigation purposes
because the irrigation sector is the sector that consumed the most water in the world.
So if we satisfy that sector of the economy and we can produce crops and food or everyone,
that will be a huge win for us and that's what we would like to achieve down the road.
This is one of the prototypes that we developed.
What we do is we develop these units.
They are simply connected to the open water surface.
We allow the water to be in communication with the cylinder here in the middle.
So what happens?
The sun will basically penetrate the structure and evaporate some of the water.
Eventually, when the temperature goes down at night, the water vapour inside will condense naturally.
We now know that we have a clear path for us as a startup and a technology developer
of how to bring this technology to customers on a large scale.
And we believe that if you provide an inexpensive way of producing water for customers,
that will help alleviate the challenges when it comes to water security across the globe.

youtube_description:
The Actionists from Abu Dhabi-based startup, Manhat, have created a floating water desalination platform, powered by solar energy. 

Water evaporating from the surface of the ocean is captured, condensed, and collected as fresh water — mimicking the natural water cycle and can avoid the usual desalination by-product of brine. Combined with greenhouse-like structures, the water can be used to irrigate crops, enabling the platforms to become floating, off-grid farms. 

Join a 🌍 of #Actionism at cop28.com/action #COP28UAE
